title: How Sunlight Becomes Electricity
audience: Curious 8–14 year olds and general YouTube viewers; 16:9, ~40 s
fact_check: Photovoltaic effect: absorbed photons free electrons in silicon → direct current (DC).
Inverters convert DC to alternating current (AC) used by household outlets and the grid.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Pip! Ever wondered how sunshine can light up a whole city?
It starts with tiny packets of light called photons, racing all the way from the sun.
When photons hit a solar panel, they knock electrons loose inside the silicon.
Those moving electrons make an electric current.
An inverter changes that current into the kind our homes can use.
Then power lines carry it into town, and the whole city lights up!
Sunlight in, electricity out. Pretty bright idea, right?
